title: Derived maps from locally finite free sheaves via hypercohomology
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,R)$ be a ringed site small under [def-weil-size-convention], with module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $P$ be an $R$-module sheaf such that every site object admits a covering on which $P$ is isomorphic to $R^{\oplus r}$ for finite nonnegative $r$ (ranks may vary between covering objects). Define $P^\vee=\mathcal Hom_R(P,R)$ using [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. For every bounded-below complex $K^\bullet$ of $R$-module sheaves and every integer $n$ there is a canonical isomorphism of abelian groups $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(P[0],QK[n])\cong H^n(R\Gamma(\mathcal C,P^\vee\otimes_R K^\bullet))$, where tensor is termwise sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], $Q$ is localization, and derived global sections are computed by a bounded-below injective resolution. The isomorphism is natural in $P$, in $K$, and in shifts; it is induced by evaluation $P^\vee\otimes_RP\to R$.

proof.text: Use the canonical closed-category comparison P-dual tensor N to internal Hom(P,N). The generic-site comparison theorem identifies it with sheafification of the presheaf evaluation map. A finite local generating family for P gives a finite free presentation on covering objects; the existing dual-basis bijectivity theorem proves sectionwise bijectivity after every restriction over a covering object. Local injectivity and surjectivity imply the presheaf map belongs to the sheafification localizer, so sheafification makes it invertible. This works also for rank zero and varying local ranks.

proof.text: Internal Hom(P,-) is right adjoint to tensor(P,-). Tensor(P-dual,-) is naturally isomorphic to it by step 1, hence preserves limits, and is itself a left adjoint, hence preserves colimits. It is therefore exact. Apply the same argument to the locally finite free dual of P and use the canonical bidual isomorphism to show tensor(P,-) exact. The tensor-Hom adjunction with exact left adjoint makes internal Hom(P,-) preserve K-injective complexes. Transport this property to tensor(P-dual,-). These are the existing sheaf tensor-Hom adjunction, dual local-freeness and bidual APIs, and Mathlib preservation-of-K-injectives API.

proof.text: For any abelian category, identify the Hom complex from the complex concentrated in degree zero at P with the ordinary complex Hom(P,K^i), using Mathlib Cochain.fromSingleEquiv and its differential formula. Mathlib CohomologyClass.homAddEquiv identifies its zeroth homology additively with homotopy classes of maps P[0] to K. Prove the cycle formula using the canonical cycles-to-cohomology-class map. Prove naturality by lifting a homology class to a cycle, representing its class by a chain map, and applying the cycle formula after precomposition and postcomposition.

proof.text: For K-injective K, the evaluation isomorphisms of step 1 give an isomorphism of complexes from global cochains of P-dual tensor K to Hom(P,K). Tensor(P-dual,-) preserves K-injectives by step 2, so the ordinary-to-derived global cohomology comparison is invertible by the existing right-derived-functor fully-faithfulness theorem. Mathlib Qh_map_bijective identifies homotopy maps into K with derived maps. Their composite gives the desired additive equivalence for K-injectives. The cycle formula of step 3 proves the stipulated evaluation normalization, and functoriality of the comparison proves naturality in both variables. The Lean argument is formulated for an abstract abelian monoidal category with additive tensor functors, comparison isomorphisms and exact tensor by P; specializing these inputs to sheaves avoids expanding sheafification during the homological proof.

proof.text: Use the existing constructed functorial K-injective resolution I and its natural quasi-isomorphism eta. Define the equivalence for arbitrary K by postcomposition with Q(eta_K), followed by the K-injective equivalence for I(K), followed by the inverse of hypercohomology applied to Q(tensor(P-dual,eta_K)). Exactness from step 2 makes the last morphism invertible. Naturality of eta and the termwise tensor square prove naturality of this composite. If K is already K-injective, naturality of the K-injective equivalence along eta_K proves equality with the equivalence of step 4, so its cycle normalization follows. No boundedness hypothesis is needed in the construction; specialize to the original bounded-below statement. Applying the degree-zero statement to shifts is exactly the formulation used by the unchanged target.
